body.statement: For either globally defined Moore--Penrose comparator \(b\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\), \[\Delta(b)=E_P[(b-b^{\star}(X))^{\prime}\Gamma(X)(b-b^{\star}(X))].\] Under the separated positive spectrum on the contrast range, \(\Delta(b)=0\) if and only if \[d_{\mathrm{cmp}}(X)=N^{\prime}\Gamma(X)b=0\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.\] Thus the published OVS loading and the best joint constant loading are efficient exactly when each satisfies its own pointwise projection equations; unconditional cancellation is insufficient. The observable plug-in residual is \(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\), with each comparator recomputed by the same Moore--Penrose KKT and minimum-norm convention.
body.justification: The pointwise equations give a falsifiable equality frontier rather than a generic claim that conditional weighting helps.
body.gap: The banked constant-loading parent derives only an unconditional normal equation, and Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025) do not characterize equality with the conditional efficiency bound.
body.consumer: An empirical diagnostic can determine whether the published package backend already attains the bound at the fitted law.
